## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Sources disagree about the best tide.
- No survey, scientific or official source describes the shape of the bottom.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the swell period this break needs.

|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | High | Supported by 5 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Low | Supported by one source (a community source); 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Wind | High | Supported by 6 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry; 1 disagrees. |
| Tide | Low | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide; 4 disagree. |

| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 5 independent sources, including an encyclopedia entry. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind agrees with the profile (120 deg): southeast trades (Wikipedia, WSL 2022 preview, World Surfaris) and east (Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia); Indonesian Surf Guide's E-NE (67.5 deg) is the only outlier. Tide is still the main conflict and leans away from low_to_mid: high (Wikipedia 'bigger and better at high tide'; World Surfaris for swells of 8 ft+ and for Speedies), mid to high (Indonesian Surf Guide), mid (Surf-Forecast), all tides (Surf Indonesia); only World Surfaris' personal tip ('surf Money Trees on low tide') supports low, and Wikipedia says barrels get more critical as the tide drops and low tide at Speedies can be very dangerous. Size: Wikipedia gives Moneytrees as 2-10 ft Hawaiian (about 4-20 ft faces) and Indonesian Surf Guide head high to triple overhead+, so the profile's 15 ft maximum looks low; its 4 ft minimum matches Wikipedia. Period: Indonesian Surf Guide 14-18 s (and Surfer Today, unread, about 14 s), consistent with the profile's 13 s minimum and 16 s ideal. Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia) and S-SW (WSL 2022, Indonesian Surf Guide), inside the profile window. Reef length conflict: Wikipedia half a kilometre (rideable point over 1 km), WSL 1.5 km. Season: April-September (Wikipedia), April-October (Surf Indonesia), May-October (Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide), all consistent with the profile. The earlier WSL claims were on the 2022 preview, not post 453801 (now magazine type, with only the section description). Both ResearchGate items return 403 and are kept from search evidence; Crossref shows the Plengkung marketing paper (Jurnal Kebijakan Pembangunan, 2021, DOI 10.47441/jkp.v16i2.201), but its abstract does not contain the April-October claim and the journal PDF timed out. No surf-break or bathymetry study and no Alas Purwo National Park page with conditions were found.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 4 ft (face) | documented | S1 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | relative face: head high to triple overhead+; swell: 4–12 ft · mixed (see value) | documented | S8 | no separate setting; working range 4–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 20 ft (face) | documented | S1 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: Wikipedia says Moneytrees works from about 2 ft Hawaiian scale, which the article itself gives as about 4 ft wave faces.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “Moneytrees works from about 2 to 10 feet (Hawaiian scale, or about 4 to 20 feet wave faces)”
- **Ideal range**: The Indonesian Surf Guide gives the wave size as head high to triple overhead+ (relative face height) and the best swell as a solid S-SW swell of 4-12+ ft (a swell figure, open at the top); no conversion between the two is stated.
  - S8 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Wave size | Head high to triple overhead+”
  - S8 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “Solid S–SW swell, 4–12+ ft, long period (14–18s)”
- **Maximum suitable**: Wikipedia says Moneytrees works up to about 10 ft Hawaiian scale, which it gives as about 20 ft faces; the Indonesian Surf Guide's 'triple overhead+' is open-ended.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “Moneytrees works from about 2 to 10 feet (Hawaiian scale, or about 4 to 20 feet wave faces)”

  - S2 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “is an exposed reef break that has very consistent waves”
  - S5 (Surfer Today): “One article calls G-Land one of the most exposed reefs in Indonesia, catching more swell than any other break.”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Stretching along one and a half kilometers of exposed reef, it catches significant swell, with different sections and take-off spots.”
  - S10 (World Surfaris): “It's no secret that G-Land is a swell magnet”

- **Break type**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break and Wikipedia describes long lefts peeling along shallow coral reef.
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “is an exposed reef break that has very consistent waves”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “which peel at a rapid rate along a half-kilometer stretch of shallow coral reef”
- **Orientation**: Wikipedia says the break has a westerly aspect at right angles to the predominant swell direction, so swell wraps around the point.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “it has a westerly aspect; i.e. at right angles to the predominant swell direction. As a result, swell wraps around the point and into the eastern side of the bay”
- **Exposure**: Surfer Today (search summary) calls it one of the most exposed reefs in Indonesia, and Surf-Forecast and WSL call the reef exposed.
  - S5 (Surfer Today): “One article calls G-Land one of the most exposed reefs in Indonesia, catching more swell than any other break.”
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast (surf-forecast.com)): “is an exposed reef break that has very consistent waves”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Stretching along one and a half kilometers of exposed reef, it catches significant swell, with different sections and take-off spots.”
- **Bathymetry**: Wikipedia describes a half-kilometre stretch of shallow coral reef and WSL 1.5 km of exposed reef (a length disagreement), the Indonesian Surf Guide a massive reef shelf that bends the swell, ResearchGate (search summary) coral reef extending into the open sea, and Surf Indonesia a 10,000 ft drop-off a few miles away; no survey is cited.
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “which peel at a rapid rate along a half-kilometer stretch of shallow coral reef”
  - S4 (World Surf League): “Stretching along one and a half kilometers of exposed reef, it catches significant swell, with different sections and take-off spots.”
  - S8 (Ultimate Indonesian Surf Guide (indonesiansurfguide.com)): “the wave unloads over a massive reef shelf that bends swell into a series of world-class left-hand sections”
  - S6 (ResearchGate): “organic corals form on the Plengkung coast, and the reef formation spreads along the coastline and extends into the open sea”
  - S9 (Surf Indonesia (surfindonesia.com)): “Thanks to a 10,000 foot drop off a few miles from the edge of Grajagan”

## Conflicting information

- **Wind · offshore**: Wikipedia, WSL and World Surfaris give the southeast trades (135 deg) and Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia and Surfer Today (search summary) east or east to southeast (90-135 deg), while the Indonesian Surf Guide says E-NE trades groom it (67.5 deg, 67.5 deg from southeast).
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Wikipedia says the waves are bigger and better at high tide and World Surfaris says you need a good high tide (and high tide for Speedies), the Indonesian Surf Guide says mid to high varying by section, Surf-Forecast says mid, Surf Indonesia all tides, and World Surfaris' own tip is to surf Money Trees at low tide.
